page: Amazon Web Services m5zn.xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-hypervised virtual machine configured with high clock frequency x86_64 compute. Powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8252C processor capable of sustained all-core clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz, the instance delivers 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is provisioned at 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3.0 GHz, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction flags include AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI), AES-NI, and BMI2. The instance does not include integrated local SSD storage or GPU acceleration, and operates with a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark outcomes show that single-threaded throughput is a major asset for this instance. In single-threaded gzip compression, the instance achieved 31.77 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated systems. Geekbench single-core testing reached 1535.0 and stress-ng single-core registered 1865.28, both falling into the middle 50% performance bracket. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics are limited by the physical core count of two, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 3341.0 and stress-ng multi-core recording 4916.36, both falling into the bottom 25%. Similarly, high-concurrency tasks like Clang software compilation (4689.0), ray tracing (3650.0), and Redis SET throughput (5.29 million ops/sec) reflect constraints common to smaller multi-threaded configurations.

The m5zn.xlarge represents a focused tradeoff, prioritizing single-core clock rate over broad core parallelism. Because it lacks bundled local disks, persistence and storage operations rely entirely on Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS). It is technically suited for workloads that depend primarily on low-latency single-thread execution, moderate memory, and vector acceleration, such as light web serving, single-threaded batch compression, continuous integration runner stages, and small-footprint enterprise backends.

It offers a 5 Gbps baseline network interface without included local storage or GPU hardware. The server excels in single-threaded performance, as demonstrated by a top-tier 31.77 GB/sec single-threaded gzip compression benchmark and an average Geekbench single-core score of 1535.0.
